review.title: The fail-closed deployment path is asserted by nobody, because CI runs two of three configurations
review.acceptance:
FOUND BY MEASUREMENT IN ROUND 108: the development and production suites were both run to completion and their SKIP LISTS intersected. Five e2e titles are skipped in BOTH, so no configuration this repository executes ever runs them. Two are media-rig rows that correctly need the commander's hardware. THE OTHER THREE ASSERT A FAIL-CLOSED SECURITY BEHAVIOUR: 'a deployment with no identity system - fails closed with 503 and names the operator's remedy', '- publishes nothing only a resolver could know' (playback-session.api.spec.ts), and 'a deployment with no identity system refuses honestly rather than showing an empty list' (watchlist.spec.ts).

They need PRODUCTION MODE WITH NO DATABASE -- the third configuration. ci.yml runs exactly two: development, and production with PostgreSQL. The tests are not broken: run locally in that third configuration the full chromium+api suite gives 62 passed / 56 skipped / 0 failed.

REQUIRED: the third configuration runs in CI and fails the build when it fails.
REQUIRED: the cost is stated rather than absorbed. A third suite run adds to every push; the acceptance is that the fail-closed path is covered, not that it is covered in the most expensive available way. If a narrower invocation -- the three titles, or the two specs -- buys the same coverage for less, take it and say why.
REQUIRED: the three titles actually EXECUTE in the new configuration. Evidence is the run naming them as passed, not a count that went up.
REQUIRED: the two media-rig titles stay skipped and stay reasoned. They are RIG rows in PW-0601's matrix and must not be made to look covered.
REQUIRED: no existing configuration loses coverage, and no skip loses its reason.

OUT OF SCOPE: changing what the three tests assert, and relaxing any of them to make a cheaper configuration reach them.
review.notes:
CREATED IN ROUND 108. DEPENDS ON PL-0714 because that task owns .github/workflows/ci.yml and is in REVIEW; editing the file from here while it is an active surface would be the overlapping-surface collision the operating model forbids. Sequenced, not blocked.

THE PATTERN THIS IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE OF, recorded so the next one is found by a check rather than by accident: scripts/test-validate-repo.mjs ran nowhere until PL-AI-0002; scripts/test-desktop-target.mjs and the 30-case Windows lifecycle suite ran nowhere until PL-0714; apps/web/src/components/player/tracks.ts was imported by nothing until PW-0306 wired it. Each time the thing existed, passed, and no gate asked it. A standing mechanical check for 'skipped in every configuration we run' would have found all four, and proposing one is a reasonable thing for this task's implementation to consider -- the measurement that found this was two suite runs and a set intersection.

CONFLICT-CHECKED IN BOTH FIELDS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT FILING: .github/workflows/ci.yml is held by PL-0714 (REVIEW) and by PL-0001, PL-0704, PL-AI-0002 and PW-0312, all DONE. The dependency on PL-0714 is what keeps the two from being active together. The reviewDependencies are read-only here: e2e/tests/watchlist.spec.ts belongs to PL-0715 (REVIEW) and is NOT written by this task.

e2e.evidence:
THE THIRD CONFIGURATION RUNS, THE THREE TITLES EXECUTE IN IT, AND THE GUARD THAT SAYS SO WAS PROVEN TO REFUSE.

MEASURED FIRST, DECIDED SECOND. All three configurations were run to completion locally with a JSON reporter and their executed sets compared:

  development              ran 122  skipped 29   274.8s
  production + PostgreSQL  ran 100  skipped 51    99.0s
  production, NO database  ran  71  skipped 80    75.4s

Tests the third configuration runs that NEITHER other one does -- computed as C minus (A union B), not asserted -- are EXACTLY three:
  [api]      playback-session.api.spec.ts > a deployment with no identity system > fails closed with 503 and names the operator's remedy
  [api]      playback-session.api.spec.ts > a deployment with no identity system > publishes nothing only a resolver could know
  [chromium] watchlist.spec.ts > a deployment with no identity system refuses honestly rather than showing an empty list

Tests skipped in ALL THREE once this step exists: exactly two, both media-rig rows. They are RIG rows in PW-0601's matrix, they need the commander's hardware, and they remain skipped with their reasons intact -- which the acceptance requires and which this measurement confirms rather than hopes.

THE NARROW INVOCATION WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, WITH THE REASON. The acceptance invites naming the two spec files if that buys the same coverage for less. It was measured: the dominant cost is the production build, which either invocation pays and turbo serves from cache in this job, leaving 75 seconds of test time. Against that, naming two files would put a hand-maintained list of what matters into this workflow -- the same defect PL-0714 removed from the suite steps above it and PL-0726 removed from the migration step below it, in this very file, this round and last. A future test that became third-configuration-only would be covered by the whole-suite step and missed by the narrow one, silently, which is precisely how these three were lost for eight rounds.

THE RUN. `npm test -- --project=api --project=chromium --reporter=list,json,html` with LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=production and NO LIBERTY_E2E_DATABASE_URL. The absence is the configuration: src/env.ts derives the auth secret from that variable's presence, so a production run without it IS a deployment with no identity system. Nothing is stubbed and no test is told it is special.

`html` IS NAMED ON THE COMMAND LINE DELIBERATELY, and finding out why was a defect caught before commit: --reporter on the CLI REPLACES the config's reporter list rather than adding to it, so the first draft wrote no e2e/playwright-report at all and the upload step would have archived nothing. Verified after the fix: both /tmp/verify-reporters.json and e2e/playwright-report/index.html are produced.

THE GUARD, AND THE FIVE WAYS IT WAS PROVEN TO REFUSE. The acceptance says evidence must be "the run naming them as passed, not a count that went up", so a step reads the JSON report and requires all three BY NAME, each present and each "expected". It was extracted from the workflow with yaml.safe_load -- so what was executed is the text CI will execute -- and driven against real reports:

  A. the real third-configuration report      -> exit 0, three "ran and passed" notices naming each title and its project
  B. the real production+PostgreSQL report    -> exit 1, three errors, each saying the title is "skipped", not "expected"
  C. the real development report              -> exit 1, three errors
  D. a report with one title renamed          -> exit 1, "No test matching ... is in the report at all. It was renamed or deleted"
  E. no report file at all                    -> exit 1, "whether these three ran is unknown -- which is not the same as them having run"

B and C are the important ones: the guard is driven against the two configurations CI ACTUALLY RUNS TODAY and goes red on both. It would have caught the original defect. A sixth case arrived unplanned while verifying the reporters -- a run of only playback-session.api.spec.ts -- and it refused on the missing watchlist title.

The step also emits the suite counts as an annotation, because annotations are the only CI channel this session can read.

NOTHING WAS WEAKENED. No test was changed, no assertion relaxed, no skip removed, no retry added, no timeout raised. The two existing suite steps are untouched -- `git diff` over this file is confined to the inserted block -- so no existing configuration loses coverage.

review.title: An LGPL-compatible libmpv and FFmpeg the product may actually ship
review.acceptance: The libmpv and FFmpeg binaries the installer ships are built under terms this product may distribute, and the evidence is recorded rather than assumed. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 9 names two traps and RESEARCH_PLAYBACK.md already found the equivalent defect elsewhere -- 'every prebuilt ffprobe on npm is a GPL-3.0 binary, and several declare otherwise' -- so a downloaded build is not evidence of its own licence. REQUIRED: the configure flags that keep the build LGPL are stated and reproducible, and any GPL-only component is named and excluded. REQUIRED: the written-offer and attribution obligations LGPL imposes on a shipped binary are satisfied by something in the installer, not by a sentence in a README nobody ships. REQUIRED: the exact upstream versions are pinned and recorded, because PW-0207's error mapping is built against a specific header. NOT IN SCOPE: any decoder whose distribution needs a patent licence this project does not hold -- if one is required, stop and report it as a commander decision rather than shipping it.

review.title: Settings a viewer can actually change
review.acceptance: There is a settings screen, and every switch on it changes something real. Neither a screen nor an API exists today. REQUIRED: preferred audio and subtitle languages, persisted per profile and consumed as PW-0206's defaults rather than as a second policy. REQUIRED: a diagnostics and telemetry control that is honest about what it does -- telemetry-decision.ts already reports WHY telemetry is off, and that reasoning belongs in front of the viewer instead of in a details element in the player. REQUIRED: an about section naming the application version and the licences the installer must carry, which is where PW-0208's LGPL attribution obligation is discharged in the product. REQUIRED: no setting weakens a security or rights control; there is no 'allow insecure sources' switch and no way to disable the transport checks.

unit.evidence:
npx vitest run apps/web: 95 files, 1714 tests, 0 failures. The whole repository under npx vitest run apps/web packages/contracts packages/persistence: 119 files, 2262 passed, 1 skipped.

WHAT THIS TASK ADDED OR CHANGED, AND WHAT EACH ONE IS FOR:

apps/web/src/components/settings/settings.test.tsx -- 13 cases, new. The language field's PARSE is pinned over the five inputs that matter: order preserved ("ja, en, de"), whitespace and empties dropped but never a tag, an empty field answering [] rather than [""] (which would reach the endpoint and be refused for something the viewer did not type), a lossless round trip with formatLanguageList, and case left alone because the ENDPOINT owns what a language tag is and a client that lower-cased first would be a second validator whose message a viewer never sees. Two source rules on the form: it mentions no profileId anywhere (the endpoint derives the profile from the session and its contract is .strict(), so the component could not address another household's settings even by accident), and it applies state from the RESPONSE on both paths rather than from the inputs. The diagnostics section is asserted by COMPUTING decidePlaybackTelemetry independently with the same inputs and requiring the rendered page to agree, code by code -- so a change to the decision that this screen stopped reflecting fails here instead of misleading a viewer -- plus a source rule that it offers no control at all, because a toggle wired to nothing is the fake persistence the round-110 instruction forbids by name. About is asserted twice deliberately: the rendered version equals package.json's, AND the source contains no version-shaped literal, because the first assertion passes either way and only the second catches a paste.

apps/web/src/app/watch/watch-session.test.ts -- 5 cases added, 30 total, all passing. These are where the acceptance's "consumed as PW-0206's defaults" is actually proven, and they pin the three states apart: null (nobody has chosen) sends CONSERVATIVE_CAPABILITIES unchanged; a list sends it with preferredAudioLanguages replaced, IN THE VIEWER'S ORDER (asserted as a sequence, not a set -- the contract says order is meaningful); and [] sends the empty list, which is the case that forces the caller to carry `stored` rather than collapsing an opt-out into a default. A fourth pins the BLAST RADIUS -- the key set is identical to the baseline and every key except preferredAudioLanguages is unchanged, written that way so a capability field added later is covered without anybody remembering -- because every other field is a claim about what the DEVICE can decode and a settings screen must not be able to widen one. A fifth proves the list is copied, so a later mutation of the repository's array cannot change a request already described.

apps/web/src/lib/viewer-preferences.test.ts -- 3 cases, new, and the header states plainly what this environment can and cannot see. The loader resolves the REAL repository adapter and the REAL identity system, exactly as loadResumePosition does, so no store is injected and no success path is faked here. What is pinned is the property that holds in every configuration and is the one a playback page depends on: a read that cannot be satisfied answers stored:false with the neutral value rather than throwing, the direction matters (stored:true with empty lists would be an opt-out the viewer never expressed), and the shared constant it returns is frozen so one caller cannot mutate what the next render sees.

A CORRECTION MADE WHILE WRITING THIS, RECORDED BECAUSE IT WAS A REAL MISTAKE. The first draft of loadMediaPreferences returned MediaPreferences alone, with a comment arguing the stored/not-stored distinction "does not matter to the media engine". That was wrong, and the first caller proved it: an unconfigured profile must keep getting ["en"] and a cleared profile must get [], and both have empty lists. The loader now returns StoredMediaPreferences and the wrong comment is replaced by the reasoning at the same place rather than quietly deleted.

e2e.evidence:
RE-RECORDED AFTER A FLAKE IN THIS TASK'S OWN SPEC; see the defect.found event immediately before this. The product behaved correctly in every run; an unscoped getByRole("alert") collided with Next's route announcer and is now scoped to the Languages section and asserts the endpoint's own reason text.

FINAL MEASUREMENTS, ALL CHROMIUM (the only browser ci.yml installs), all --workers=1:

PRODUCTION BUILD + REAL POSTGRESQL: 88 cases, 49 passed, 39 skipped, 0 failed, 1.0m.
DEVELOPMENT BUILD: 88 cases, 67 passed, 21 skipped, 0 failed, 2.4m.
settings.spec.ts WITH --repeat-each=3 against production + PostgreSQL: 27 passed, 0 failed, 31.7s. Repeated on purpose: a flake that passes once after a fix has not been shown to be fixed.

THE NINE CASES. Group A is true in every configuration: the About version read from the real apps/web/package.json at run time rather than written into the spec; THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md named together with the sentence that the screen has not inspected your installation, because PW-0208 is the task that proves a packaged tree carries it; the diagnostics collector path and at least one real reason code on screen; and no switch that could weaken a security or rights control, asserted as an absence of the VOCABULARY ("allow insecure", "disable transport", "skip verification", "ignore certificate", "developer mode", "unsafe") rather than of a particular control id, with a non-vacuity check that the page underneath is the real one.

Group B runs against a real signed-in session and real rows. "A choice survives a reload, which is what tells persistence from state" sets the profile back to not-chosen through the API first -- so the starting state is MADE true rather than inherited -- then types ja/en, saves, and RELOADS. Everything before the reload would pass against a component that remembered the typing and never spoke to a server, which is what the round-110 instruction forbade by name. "The order is kept" saves a deliberately non-alphabetical pt-BR, ja, en and reads back the sequence. "Clearing is not the same as leaving the lists empty" saves two EMPTY lists, reloads to "these are your choices", then clears, reloads to "you have not chosen yet" -- same empty fields, opposite meanings, which is what makes the API's stored flag load-bearing. The refusal case types "english", requires the scoped alert AND its BCP-47 text AND the absence of the success sentence, then reloads to prove nothing was written. The signed-out case sets no session headers at all, so it is the real branch, and asserts the form is absent while About and Diagnostics remain.

CI CAVEAT, UNCHANGED AND STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED: group B needs profile_media_preference, which ci.yml did not create because it applied migration 0000 by name. PL-0726 fixes that, is gated against a real PostgreSQL and is in review in this same bundle. Without it this gate is local-only and CI would be red, because group B does not skip when LIBERTY_E2E_DATABASE_URL is set.

WHAT THE SPEC STILL DOES NOT CLAIM, written into its header: it does not assert that a stored language changes which audio track PLAYS. The e2e catalog is fixtures; what the preference reaches is the playback SESSION REQUEST, proven directly in watch-session.test.ts over all three states with the body parsed by the route's own strict schema.

ENVIRONMENT: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH pointed at ~/.cache/ms-playwright, because this container's /opt/pw-browsers holds revision 1194 while the pinned @playwright/test 1.62.1 wants 1234. firefox, webkit and mobile-safari are UNVERIFIED here -- binaries absent -- and are not run in CI either.

review.title: The automated half of the Windows matrix, running on Windows
review.acceptance: Every row PW-0601 marks automated runs on a windows-latest runner and fails the build when it fails. REQUIRED: the existing e2e suite runs against the DESKTOP target on Windows, not only the web target on Ubuntu -- the desktop axis is currently built on Ubuntu only, and only incidentally, because the axis defaults on and openssl happens to be installed. REQUIRED: the shell is driven end to end where the harness can reach it, and where it cannot, the row stays in the commander-machine half rather than being replaced by a unit test that proves something easier. REQUIRED: retries stay at zero, on the rule playwright.config.ts already states at length. REQUIRED: a row that is skipped says why, by name, the way the existing harness already does for the desktop and media-rig axes.
review.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. SURFACE NOTE: this task's allowedPaths name directories that do not exist yet. The evidence-based narrowing procedure applies to reconciling work already in history; for genuinely new work the surface is the smallest set of paths the acceptance can be satisfied within, and it is narrowed again from the diff before review if it turns out to be wider than what was written. OWNERSHIP RESOLVED BY RESPONSIBILITY in round 87, on gpt-architect's ruling. .github/workflows/windows.yml moved from allowedPaths to reviewDependencies: this task is the certification CONSUMER -- it needs the workflow and the artifact to EXIST and to execute its rows, which is a read relationship. PW-0501 owns the workflow because PW-0501 produces the Windows artifact. A task does not co-own a production build workflow merely because its tests run there. If this task's acceptance genuinely requires editing that workflow after PW-0501 lands, it is sequenced AFTER PW-0501 -- its dependencies already say so -- and its narrowed write surface is derived from the actual change at claim time rather than reserved now. Neither task was narrowed to defeat conflictWithActive; the surfaces follow the implementation responsibility. ROUND 107 AMENDMENT, on gpt-architect's ruling: .github/workflows/windows.yml has MOVED from reviewDependencies to allowedPaths -- allowedPaths is always part of the reviewed surface, so leaving it in both is redundant and ai:validate says so. This is the condition the round-87 note above named -- PW-0501 has landed, and the acceptance clause 'runs on a windows-latest runner and fails the build when it fails' cannot be satisfied without writing the only file that defines one. The surface was derived at claim time from the actual change, as that note required, and is the single file rather than .github/workflows/**. scripts/windows/** was deliberately NOT taken; it remains PW-0502's and PW-0503's. Conflict check and the cost to those two tasks' future fingerprints are recorded in the task.definition_changed event of this round.

typecheck.evidence:
The workflow is machine-checked by the method rounds 107-110 established. Every `run:` block with `shell: pwsh` is extracted from the YAML by a parser -- 8 blocks across both jobs, 1 new -- with ${{ runner.temp }} and every ${{ steps.<id>.outcome }} substituted as GitHub would substitute them, and each parse-checked with [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile under PowerShell 7.4.6: 0 files with parse errors. The YAML round-trips through a parser and reports jobs [package, e2e-desktop] with all fourteen package steps now carrying an id -- previously two did. npm run repo:validate passes.

THE NEW DIAGNOSTICS STEP WAS EXECUTED ON BOTH ITS BRANCHES rather than read. With every outcome "success" it emits the warning branch: "The job failed but no step reports a non-success outcome, so the failure is in the runner or in something this list does not name", followed by the full trail. With tauri-bundle set to failure and the two steps after it left empty, it emits "FIRST FAILING STEP: tauri-bundle (failure). Everything after it did not run." and the trail renders those two as not-reached -- which is exactly the sentence Windows #14 could not produce.

e2e.evidence:
WINDOWS #14 (run 37172243171, head 4a13f4593ee00aff71acb470d065c7cffa39b1a4) IS REAL EVIDENCE AND IT SETTLES THE HALF THIS TASK WAS WRITTEN FOR.

THE e2e-desktop JOB CONCLUDED SUCCESS, 3m 35s, on the first Windows execution of a job that had never run. Its annotations, verbatim: "openssl=C:\Program Files\OpenSSL\bin\openssl.exe; mode=development; database=none (GitHub service containers are Linux-only, so the production-with-identity rung stays on Ubuntu)" and "expected=118 unexpected=0 flaky=0 skipped=24 duration=134.8s".

WHY SUCCESS IS THE LOAD-BEARING FACT RATHER THAN THE COUNTS. The job contains "The desktop axis actually ran" as an ordinary failing step, running assert-desktop-axis-ran.mjs against the run's own JSON report. A Playwright run in which every desktop case skipped exits 0, so a job that merely invoked the suite could have been green while proving nothing -- that guard is what makes success mean the axis executed. It cannot have passed on an all-skipped report, because that is the one case it was built to refuse and was observed refusing locally. So: npm ci succeeded on windows-latest, the browser installed, the two Next servers and the loopback stub ran, openssl resolved without needing the Git fallback this workflow carries, and the desktop-target and cross-target API cases EXECUTED. 118 expected and 0 unexpected matches the Linux development run exactly, which is the right answer for the same suite in the same mode. Retries remain 0; nothing in this change touches playwright.config.ts.

PW-0602's first REQUIRED clause -- "the existing e2e suite runs against the DESKTOP target on Windows, not only the web target on Ubuntu" -- is met, by a run rather than by a parser.

THE PACKAGE JOB CONCLUDED FAILURE, and this round's work is about being able to say why. Its only annotations were "Process completed with exit code 1" and the lifecycle publisher's "NO REPORT WAS PRODUCED. The harness writes nothing when it refuses (wrong platform, missing or bad --msi), which is a fault in this workflow rather than in the product."

THAT SENTENCE ASSERTS A CAUSE IT CANNOT KNOW, and that is the defect repaired here. The publisher runs on !cancelled(), so it says that whenever no report file exists -- equally true if the Tauri bundle failed, if the inventory threw "no msi in the inventory", or if the verifier negative check failed. Only two of fourteen steps had an id, so nothing on the run page named the step that exited 1. A reader was invited to conclude the harness refused over a bad --msi. Windows #13 at 4f23c1d recorded F1 PASS, F3 PASS, F4 PASS, F2 not-run, so the job REGRESSED and the cause is not yet established. Every step now has an id; a "Which step failed" step names the first non-success step with the full trail; and it additionally lists every .msi and .exe actually under the bundle directory, because "tauri-bundle=success" and "there is an installer where the inventory looks for one" are different claims. The old message no longer asserts a cause.

TWO HYPOTHESES WERE ELIMINATED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT OPEN. (1) PL-0718's tsconfig exclusion of dist was a plausible cause, since the desktop target writes its generated types there: ruled out by deleting .next, dist and next-env.d.ts and running npm run build:desktop on the resulting clean tree, which exits 0 and emits a full route table. (2) The inventory-to-lifecycle path handoff was a plausible cause, since the lifecycle step joins the bundle root with the inventory's name: ruled out by reading artifact-inventory.mjs, which records name as relative(bundleDir, path) -- "msi/<file>.msi" -- so the join is correct, and which already refuses both zero and multiple installers per kind.

WHAT IS STILL UNVERIFIED AND IS NOT CLAIMED: the cause of the package failure, and therefore the lifecycle rows for this head. No row is classified as A, B, C or D on this evidence, because classifying from an annotation that admits it does not know would be guessing. The next Windows run of this workflow names the step; that is the evidence, and this gate is not it.

CHANGES REQUESTED at 4a13f4593ee00aff71acb470d065c7cffa39b1a4, under gpt-architect's own round-110 condition, transcribed by claude-test. The reviewer wrote: "Do NOT approve PW-0602 from parser-only evidence if Windows #14 has not proven the new job", and required that for lifecycle "every observable row" be verified as PASS, FAIL, NOT-RUN with an exact reason, then classified as (A) workflow/harness defect, (B) product defect, (C) commander-only row or (D) genuinely unsupported CI row.

WHAT WINDOWS #14 (run 37172243171, head 4a13f45) PROVED, AND IT IS THE HALF THIS TASK WAS WRITTEN FOR. The e2e-desktop job CONCLUDED SUCCESS in 3m 35s. Its annotations read "openssl=C:\Program Files\OpenSSL\bin\openssl.exe; mode=development; database=none" and "expected=118 unexpected=0 flaky=0 skipped=24 duration=134.8s". Success is the load-bearing fact: the job contains the non-vacuity guard as a FAILING step, so a run in which the desktop axis had skipped could not have concluded success. The desktop axis therefore genuinely executed on a Windows runner, on the first attempt, with retries still at zero and the same two projects CI runs. PW-0602's first REQUIRED clause is met.

WHY THIS CANNOT BE APPROVED ANYWAY. The package job CONCLUDED FAILURE with "Process completed with exit code 1", and the only other annotation is the lifecycle publisher's own notice: "NO REPORT WAS PRODUCED. The harness writes nothing when it refuses (wrong platform, missing or bad --msi), which is a fault in this workflow rather than in the product."

THAT NOTICE CANNOT SUPPORT THE CLASSIFICATION THE REVIEWER ASKED FOR, and that is the finding. The publisher runs on `!cancelled()`, so it emits that sentence whenever no report file exists -- which is equally true if the Tauri build failed, if the inventory step threw "no msi in the inventory", if the install-verifier negative check failed, or if the harness itself refused. Only two of the package job's fourteen steps carry an `id`, so nothing on the run page names the step that exited 1. A reader is therefore invited to conclude "the harness refused over a bad --msi" when the evidence does not establish it. That is the same defect this session has now corrected three times in its own instruments: a diagnostic confidently naming a cause it has not measured.

This is category A -- a workflow/harness defect -- but it is specifically a defect in the workflow's ABILITY TO BE DIAGNOSED, and it must be fixed before any row is classified, because classifying from this annotation would be guessing. Windows #13 at 4f23c1d recorded F1 PASS, F3 PASS, F4 PASS and F2 not-run, so the package job REGRESSED between 4f23c1d and 4a13f45 and the cause is not yet known.

REQUIRED BEFORE RE-REVIEW: every step in the package job carries an id; a failure-diagnostics step names the first failing step and its outcome on the run page, in the annotation channel, as ci.yml's own failure-diagnostics already does; and the "NO REPORT" message stops asserting a cause it cannot know.
